claims: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET.
The splashdown occurred at 5:07 p.m. PT.
The Artemis II crew landed safely.
The splashdown concluded a 10-day mission around the moon.
The landing location was the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California.
The landing time was 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II crew was retrieved by the Navy ship USS John P. Murtha for post-mission medical evaluations.
The Artemis II mission marked the first time humans traveled to the moon and returned safely since 1972.
